metadata.layer: attestations-lit — coronations reported by secondary literature, each with the author’s own citation of the Chapter archive where given
sources: Dana Vrabelová, Imago gratiosa. Korunované Madony ve střední Evropě v době baroka / Crowned Madonnas in Central Europe in the Baroque Period. Dissertation, Charles University, Prague, 2013. § XXI (p. 223), chronological table of thirty coronations by the Chapter of St Peter's in Baroque Central Europe, 1717–1786; per-image ACSP folio citations from the footnotes of her §§ X–XVII.

Nicolas Balzamo, « Uniformisation ou distinction ? Le couronnement des Madones dans l'Europe moderne (XVIIe-XVIIIe siècles) », Réforme, Humanisme, Renaissance 97 (2023), pp. 169-190. Coronations named in the text and footnotes, with his citations of BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate (volume, folio) where given.
caveats: Secondary evidence: none of these records was read at first hand; confidence is capped at medium.
Where the author cites no folio, confidence is low and the record says so.

records.act_type: Coronation reported by secondary literature
records.notes: Reported by Balzamo 2023, not read at first hand. The first image crowned under the Sforza initiative, before the count's earliest surviving letters of 1634 (p. 174); 1631 is the year of the petition per Vrabelová 2013, p. 59. Re-crowned by the Chapter in 1697 (see the tomo IV dossier).

records.act_type: Coronation reported by secondary literature, citing the Chapter dossier
register_refs: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, 7, f. 103r
records.notes: Reported by Balzamo 2023, not read at first hand. NOT EXECUTED. Petitioned by Lorenzo Boturini (memorial of 18 July 1738); the Chapter agreed, but the Council of the Indies annulled the coronation and expelled Boturini (citing Escamilla González 2010). The image was first crowned in 1895. Corrects the reading of Vrabelová 2013, p. 62, that the Chapter 'crowned' it on 1 October 1740.
